rights: No scripture text reproduced. Verse coordinates are human-curated annotations and NOT yet machine validated against the current in-app edition versification.
figures_index_target: Scripture entities must distinguish distinct people with same name; figures are discovery labels not canonical person IDs
historical_period_note: Do not infer a literal numerical year for patriarchal or Exodus narratives; biblical narrative age, historian proposed date, and commemorative liturgical year are three distinct fields. A date range is omitted in this initial evidence layer.
geolocation_note: Ancient mentions and modern physical Places are distinct; ambiguous names and symbolic sites get zero map pins; do not place a site's arbitrary region centroid as a precise spot.
authors_note: Event summaries are brief newly written descriptions. Bible references are only provisional and may require Douay/Crampon/CPDV versification crosswalks.

records.summary_en: The garden is associated with humanity's beginnings and the rivers of the Genesis narrative.
The ark comes to rest in the mountains of Ararat, a region rather than a named summit.
The tower and confusion of languages are placed in the land of Shinar.
Abraham's family departs Ur toward Haran and Canaan.
Abraham departs from Haran in response to the divine call.
Abraham reaches the oak of More; later Joshua renews the covenant at Shechem.
Jacob's dream of the ladder and his naming of Bethel are set here.
The visitors meet Abraham near Mamre; Sarah is buried in the region of Hebron.
The patriarchs dig wells and make agreements near Beersheba.
The sacrifice-of-Isaac narrative names Moriah; Chronicles associates Moriah with the Temple.
Lot's escape and the destruction of Sodom are narrated here.
Gomorrah is named with Sodom in the judgment narrative.
Joseph is taken into Egypt and the Israelites later suffer enslavement there.
Jacob's household settles in Goshen, later distinguished during the plagues.
The Israelites build a store-city named Pithom during forced labour.
One of the named store-cities and a departure point in the Exodus narrative.
The sea-crossing camp is placed near Pi-hahiroth.
The Israelites encounter bitter water which becomes drinkable.
The narrative describes twelve springs and seventy palms at Elim.
The giving of the Law and Elijah's later encounter with God are linked to Sinai or Horeb.
The spies return and Miriam dies during the wilderness period.
Aaron dies on Mount Hor according to the wilderness narrative.
Moses sees the Promised Land; his burial place remains unknown.
Joshua's crossing and Christ's Baptism belong to different places and periods along the river.
Jericho's walls fall in Joshua; Christ later meets Zacchaeus in Jericho.
Stones commemorating the passage over the Jordan are set at Gilgal.
Joshua's victory and the famous sun-and-moon narrative concern Gibeon.
The tabernacle is set up and Hannah prays for a son at the sanctuary.
Ruth's story and the birth of Christ are both associated with Bethlehem.
Samuel returns to Ramah and ministers as judge.
Saul returns to Gibeah and receives news of the threat to Jabesh.
Saul rallies Israel to relieve besieged Jabesh-gilead.
Saul and Jonathan die after the battle on Mount Gilboa.
David returns to find Ziklag raided and pursues the Amalekites.
David takes Jerusalem; later the city becomes central to Christ's Passion.
The name Zion shifts in historical usage; the Pentecost event does not establish exact Upper Room coordinates.
Elijah confronts the prophets of Baal on Carmel.
Elijah is sustained by a widow and her son is restored to life.
The northern kingdom's capital is built and later captured by Assyria.
Naboth's vineyard and Elijah's condemnation of injustice are set near Jezreel.
Barak assembles at Tabor; a later Christian tradition places the Transfiguration there.
Assyrian forces operate from Lachish during Hezekiah's reign.
Judah's deportations and Daniel's early court setting are associated with Babylon.
Ezekiel describes his vision while among the exiles by the Chebar.
Persian royal court and Nehemiah's service are located at Susa.
Jonah preaches repentance there; Tobit also lives in Nineveh in exile.
Sarah lives in Ecbatana and Tobias later journeys there.
Tobit deposits money with Gabael in Media and sends Tobias on his journey.
Judith's home town resists Holofernes' siege.
Mattathias and his family come from Modein at the start of the revolt.
Judas' forces defeat the expedition encamped near Emmaus.
Successive Temple phases frame Solomon's dedication, later desecrations and Christ's Presentation.
Christ raises Lazarus; the traditional tomb and Franciscan church are related but distinct features.
The Annunciation and Christ's synagogue reading take place in Nazareth.

records.biblical_name: Ein Karem / hill country of Judah
records.summary_en: Mary visits Elizabeth and John the Baptist is born in the Judean hill country; the exact village is traditional.
Christ calls fishermen and directs the miraculous catch near the lake.
Christ teaches, heals and works from his Galilean ministry base.
The home town of several Apostles is associated with a healing narrative.
Christ rebukes the town for not responding to his miracles.
Christ turns water into wine at a wedding; modern identification remains disputed.
Christ raises the widow's son near the gate of Nain.
The Sermon on the Mount occurs on a mountain; its present pilgrimage site is a later local tradition.
Peter confesses that Jesus is the Christ in the district of Caesarea Philippi.
Jesus speaks with the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well.
Christ heals a blind man near Jericho and encounters Zacchaeus.
Christ enters Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives area; Acts associates the Ascension with it.
The Palm Sunday entry begins near Bethphage on the Mount of Olives.
Christ prays before his arrest in a garden called Gethsemane.
The Crucifixion takes place at Golgotha, incorporated into the Holy Sepulchre complex.
Christ is buried and the empty tomb is discovered after the Resurrection.
The risen Christ joins two disciples on the way to Emmaus.
The Last Supper occurs in an upper room; Pentecost is associated in tradition with the Jerusalem community.
Saul encounters Christ on the road and is baptized in Damascus.
The disciples first receive the name Christians here and missionaries depart from the church.
Peter raises Tabitha and receives messengers from Cornelius.
Cornelius welcomes Peter and Paul later appears before Roman officials.
Paul heals a man and then suffers violence in Lystra.
Lydia is baptized and Paul and Silas are imprisoned at Philippi.
Paul preaches in the synagogue and opposition arises.
Hearers search the Scriptures to test Paul's preaching.
Paul proclaims the unknown God before Athenians at the Areopagus.
Paul works and teaches in Corinth; the Gallio hearing anchors the chronology.
Paul teaches at Ephesus and a riot arises around Artemis worship.
Paul raises Eutychus after a fall during a nighttime gathering.
Paul delivers his farewell discourse to the elders of Ephesus.
Paul meets disciples and prays with them on the shore.
Paul survives shipwreck and ministers on the island.
Paul arrives under custody and preaches in Rome.
John describes receiving his revelation while on Patmos.
The vision of the heavenly Jerusalem is theological and cannot be mapped as a present earthly site.

reference_validation.validation_scope: Canonical book, chapter ceiling, numeric verse range only; verse text, edition numbering and historical event/source relationship NOT independently reviewed

catholic_deuterocanonical_integrity.note: A book can lack explicit geographic mentions, but every occurrence must be audited; initial curated seed is not Catholic-canon exhaustive.
